$comment: One record per JSONL line in docs/ALL_FEATURES.jsonl. Developer-facing feature inventory, EN-only, single source of truth about implemented functionality. Replaces dev/FUNCTIONALITY.log; chronology comes from git history + release diffs. Public showcase lives in docs/FEATURES*.md.
title: ALL_FEATURES record

id.$comment: Stable identifier, kebab '<area>.<feature>'. It also fixes the record boundary, and S1933 draws that boundary by the gate answer rather than by the screen: a capability whose halves give different answers to 'which BuildConfig flag is this behind' is two records, because 'gate' is single-valued and validate.ps1 equates 'flavors' with that flag's row - one record spanning both answers can only lie in one of two directions. Splitting such a record keeps the old id for neither half: in both known cases the id named the very half being carved off, so a 'surviving' id would put the wrong boundary straight back into the name. The split is done when a record is next touched, not as a sweep - a spanning record only causes harm at the moment someone gives it a gate, and validate.ps1 already refuses that pairing.

area.$comment: Functional area / module, e.g. 'Video Player', 'OCR & Translation'.

name.$comment: Short EN title of the capability.

description.$comment: EN description of what the capability does.

flavors.$comment: Build variants where the capability is available. S1934 fixes how the set is derived: from the build system, never from the build the change happened to be tested on - the flag's row in docs/FLAVOR_MATRIX.md when the capability sits behind a gate, and the full six when nothing gates it, because a capability nothing narrows cannot be narrower than the app. A set that is neither the full six nor equal to some flag's row claims a reach the build system does not produce; validate.ps1 counts those against a ratchet baseline rather than refusing each one, since 242 records predate the rule. A capability living entirely in the wear module carries the full six: that module declares no flavors, the watch app is its own installation, and no phone build excludes it - any narrower set asserts an exclusion the build does not have. A watch capability that does need the phone bridge is gated by SUPPORT_WEAR_COMPANION instead.

gate.$comment: S1929. The BuildConfig flag this capability lives behind, e.g. 'SUPPORT_WEAR_COMPANION'. OPTIONAL, and its absence is an assertion rather than an omission: it means the capability is behind no flag at all, which is why documentation-only and watch-standalone records carry no gate and keep their own flavor sets. When present, scripts/all_features/validate.ps1 requires 'flavors' to equal that flag's row in docs/FLAVOR_MATRIX.md exactly, and a flag the matrix does not list is an error rather than a skip - a typo must not silently switch the check off. S1982 admits one shape beyond a single name: flags joined by '+' are a CONJUNCTION, meaning the capability needs every named flag at once, and 'flavors' must then equal the intersection of their rows exactly. Live-stream casting is the shape it exists for - the stream comes from SUPPORT_STREAMS, the receiver from SUPPORT_CAST, and neither row alone is true of it. This is still not a list of alternatives: no syntax here ever means 'any of these flags', because a capability sitting behind two different answers is two capabilities, or a record boundary drawn in the wrong place (S1933). Term order is the author's and is not normalised; a repeated term is an error, since it narrows nothing and only hides a mistyped second flag.

spec.$comment: Provenance: source spec ticket id, or null when not spec-tracked.

status.$comment: Lifecycle state of the record. Defaults to 'active'.
